items.title: Wycliffe Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001

ctx.x: I guess. But I mean and one of the great things about, I didn’t get a chance to meet all of these guys, but their personalities are just so great, they’re great people. Like I said Louis Armstrong is my, I would say is my, the one, if I had to choose one person that was most influential in jazz slash music to me I would have to say it was Louis Armstrong. But guys that played with him, Quentin “Butter” Jackson. I know he was another great trombone player. And he was also another one of the great plunger mute men.…

Hmmm? Not Slide. It’s not Al Grey, I can’t think of it. It’s going to come to me in a second. Oh, Tyree Glenn. I can never think of why I always get tied up with his name, Tyree. He played with Louis Armstrong. He was a great trombonist also. And I called all of those names, I think they all influenced me because at one point I spent time studying their style of playing or a particular solo that they may have done.
